transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess I came in because I’m just… exhausted. Like, I’m so tired I can barely make it through my shifts at the register. It’s not normal tired, it’s like my whole body is full of wet sand or something. I try to rest, and it just doesn’t really bring me back.

And it’s weird because I used to handle standing there all day, scanning groceries and making small talk—some people buy the strangest combinations of things, like yesterday this guy bought only pickles and birthday candles—but anyway, yeah… I’m just really, really tired.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… sort of. I don’t know if I’d call it “depressed” exactly, but everything feels kind of flat. Like I usually love cooking for myself, you know, making a real dinner instead of just cereal or whatever, and lately even that feels like too much and also pointless.

And my guitar’s just sitting there. I keep meaning to pick it up because I used to play after work, little songs, nothing fancy, but then I see it and I’m like… eh. Same with hiking, going over to my family’s place—stuff I normally care about. It’s like I’m pretending to be interested, but I’m not really feeling it.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t like saying it out loud, but yes. I’ve had thoughts like… maybe people would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. Which sounds dramatic, and I don’t mean it like— I don’t know.

And a few times walking home, waiting at the corner, I caught myself thinking about just stepping off the curb into traffic. Then I’d get freaked out because a bus goes by and it’s so loud, and I’m standing there thinking about how the city really should fix that crosswalk light because it takes forever… but yeah. Those thoughts have been there, and they scare me.
Did all of this start after something stressful happened in your life?

Kind of, yeah. I mean, I don’t know if it was one big stressful thing, but it started around when the store changed all our hours because of the remodel. That was about a month ago.

They moved everything around too, like the bread aisle was suddenly where the seasonal candy used to be, and customers kept asking me where things were like I personally designed the layout… but yeah, the timing was around then. This whole thing’s been going on maybe a month.
When your work stress eases up, do you still feel this flat and exhausted?

Yeah… even when it’s not as busy, I still feel wiped out. That’s actually kind of why I came in, because I’m so tired I can barely get through a shift.

It’s like my whole body is filled with wet sand or something, like my arms and legs are heavy, and then I’ll rest or sleep or just sit on the couch and it doesn’t really… recharge me. I keep thinking, okay, if work calms down I’ll feel better, but I don’t really bounce back.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah… my sleep’s been really messed up. When they started changing my shifts around, I got into this thing where I’d only sleep a few hours, but I still felt wired, like my body didn’t get the memo that it was supposed to be tired.

And now it’s weird because I am exhausted, but I’ll wake up really early and my mind is already going, like it’s been waiting for me to open my eyes. I’ll be thinking about stupid stuff too, like whether I forgot to buy detergent, or that one customer who argued about a coupon… but yeah, I’m not sleeping right.
Before this past month, have you ever had another period like this where you felt down and lost interest in things for at least two weeks?

Before this past month? Um… I guess the down part didn’t really start just this month, if I’m being honest. It’s been more like… four months of feeling low and kind of empty.

The busy work stuff made it more obvious, I think, because at first there was this rush, like I was running on whatever, and then that passed but the low feeling stayed. Like, long after the work energy wore off, I was still just… flat. And I kept telling myself it was just because of the schedule, but it’s been going on longer than that.
Before these past four months, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest in things for at least two weeks?

I don’t know… I mean, I’ve had rough times before, like everybody, I guess. Like when I was younger I’d get in these moods, but I don’t know if it was two full weeks or just a few bad days strung together.

It’s hard for me to measure it like that, honestly. I remember more what was going on around it, like work stuff or family arguments, or just feeling like I needed to sleep for a year… but I can’t really say, “yes, that was definitely two weeks.” I’m not sure.
Before these last four months, was there ever a time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day for two weeks or longer?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I can pin it down before the last four months exactly. But now, definitely, things I usually love just feel… kind of flat.

Like cooking for myself, I used to actually enjoy that—trying new recipes and all that. Or playing guitar, hiking, going over to my family’s place. Now it’s like I’m doing the motions, or I’m pretending I care because I know I’m supposed to. It just doesn’t feel the same.
Before this current stretch, was there ever a time in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Before this stretch… I’m not really sure. I keep thinking about right now, because it’s so obvious now. Like, things I usually love—cooking for myself, playing guitar, hiking, even going over to my family’s place—they just feel flat. Like I’m doing them because I’m supposed to, or pretending I care.

Before this, I don’t know if it was that steady every day for two weeks. I mean, I’ve had times where I didn’t feel like myself, but I can’t really separate it out in my head the way you’re asking.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?

Yeah… kind of. With my shifts changing around at work, it got to where I’d only sleep a few hours and still feel totally wired, like I should be exhausted but I wasn’t.

And now it’s weird because even when I am tired, I’ll wake up really early and my mind is already going. Like before I even look at the clock, I’m thinking about a hundred things. The schedule at the store doesn’t help either, they keep moving people around and then I’m up at odd times… but yeah, the sleep thing has definitely been happening.
During that time when you felt wired on only a few hours of sleep, did you also feel unusually happy or euphoric?

Yeah… at first I did. Like, weirdly cheerful, almost too good, like I could handle anything and nobody could really slow me down.

But it wasn’t just happy, if that makes sense. I’d be at work and feel like I was on top of everything, and then if someone asked me to count a drawer again or questioned something small, I’d just snap. Like way harder than the situation called for. It’s embarrassing thinking about it, because I didn’t feel like I was being unreasonable in the moment.
During that time when you felt unusually cheerful and needed very little sleep, were you more active than usual?

Yeah, definitely more active. I mean, at work I wasn’t just doing my cashier stuff—I volunteered for extra cash-office work, and then I started reorganizing shelves because they looked “wrong” to me. I even made this whole promotion binder, like with ideas and sections and everything, which… nobody asked me to do.

And then I’d go home and I still wouldn’t feel done. I’d be online looking at things to buy, thinking I should redo the apartment layout or move furniture around. It felt productive at the time, but looking back it was a lot.
About how long did that unusually energetic, cheerful, low-sleep period last?

Um… I think it’s been about a month now. It kind of started when the store changed all our hours around for the remodel, because everybody’s shifts got weird and the whole place was a mess with aisles moved and signs everywhere. So yeah, since then—about a month, I guess.
